title: Copyous crashes gnome-shell on boot/login with GNOME 50.1 (Wayland)
body:
**Environment**
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04
- Kernel: 7.0.0-29-generic
- GNOME Shell: 50.1
- Mesa: 26.0.3
- Display server: Wayland
- GPU: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT
- Copyous version: 2.0.1

**Behaviour**
After every reboot or logout, GNOME Shell crashes to a grey screen with only the cursor visible. Disabling Copyous fixes the issue immediately. Re-enabling it in a live session works fine — the crash only happens on fresh boot/login.

Confirmed through trial and error of all installed extensions:

- All extensions enabled → crashes on boot
- All extensions disabled → boots perfectly
- Copyous enabled, all others disabled → crashes again on next boot
- Copyous disabled, all others enabled → boots perfectly

Reproduced across multiple reboots consistently.

**When it started**
This issue began after system updates applied on August 5th, 2025. 
The extension worked fine before that date. 

**Other active extensions (all confirmed working)**
- blur-my-shell@aunetx
- color-picker@tuberry
- gsconnect@andyholmes.github.io
- just-perfection-desktop@just-perfection
- nightthemeswitcher@romainvigier.fr
- quick-settings-tweaks@qwreey
- quicksettings-audio-devices-hider@marcinjahn.com
- soft-brightness-plus@joelkitching.com
- text-extractor@aditya190803
- tilingshell@ferrarodomenico.com
- weatheroclock@CleoMenezesJr.github.io

title: Blur my panel added pop up blur, pls add support for it
body:

it turn every popup into blury one and beautiful, and all of my extensions that use pop up, work fine with it
except copyous, can u pls add support to it?

title: Replace LShift+Insert with RShift+Insert for paste to terminal
body:
Hello!

Replace LShift+Insert with RShift+Insert for avoid replace layout in gnome-terminal when Ctrl+LShift use like:
`gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.wm.keybindings switch-input-source ['<Control>Shift_L', '<Shift>Control_L', 'XF86Keyboard']`

The second likely reason is that on the keyboard, the right shift key is located closer to insert than the left one. And I almost never used the left shift key with insert to insert, preferring the right shift key.
However, the replacement was only enough for me in the case of the terminal. I haven't had any problems anywhere else. Therefore, I do not propose to replace the left shift with the right one in other places.

Cheers!

title: fix: make toggle pinned search shortcut configurable
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `toggle-pinned-search-shortcut` setting (default `<Alt>`) so users can change or disable the pinned-items search filter shortcut from preferences
- Replaces hardcoded Alt key detection with proper accelerator matching via `ShortcutManager`, so Alt pressed as part of another combo no longer toggles the pinned filter

## Problem

I changed the default open shortcut to **Ctrl+Alt+C**. Opening the dialog worked fine, but closing it was frustrating: pressing Alt as part of that combo also toggled the pinned-items search filter, because the pinned shortcut was hardcoded to fire on any Alt keypress regardless of other modifiers. There was no way to change or remove that shortcut in preferences — "Toggle Pinned Search" was shown as read-only.

This fix lets you rebind or disable the pinned filter shortcut (Backspace in the editor disables it), and Alt is only treated as the pinned shortcut when it matches the configured binding — not when it's one key in Ctrl+Alt+C.

## Test plan

- [ ] Open Copyous settings → Shortcuts → Search and confirm "Toggle Pinned Search" is editable; set it to `<Alt>` and verify it still toggles the pin filter in the search bar
- [ ] Press Backspace in the shortcut editor to disable the shortcut; confirm Alt no longer toggles the pinned filter
- [ ] Set the open dialog shortcut to `Ctrl-Alt-C`; open and close the dialog with that combo and confirm the pinned filter is not toggled
- [ ] Set a custom shortcut (e.g. `Ctrl-Shift-p`) and confirm it toggles the pinned filter as expected

title: Show installed build version in General settings
body: ## Why When testing perf PRs locally (`make install`, switch branches, logout/login), there is no reliable way to confirm which build is actually running. `gnome-extensions info` can show a stale version after install, and on Wayland disable/enable does not always reload GJS modules — so you can think you are on PR #138 or #135 and still be measuring the wrong code. This adds a **Version** section at the top of General settings so PR and local builds are identifiable at a glance via `git describe` metadata, with the branch name appended for non-`main` builds. A copy button lets you grab the full build string without selecting text in the row. ## Summary - Adds a **Version** section at the top of the General settings tab showing the installed build string from extension metadata. - Appends the current git branch name to `version-name` in dev builds (when not on `main`/`master`) so local and PR installs are easy to tell apart. - Adds a copy button on the version row that copies the build string to the clipboard and shows a toast confirmation. ## Test plan - [ ] `make install` on a feature branch and open Copyous settings → General — version string includes branch name (e.g. `2.0.1-7+f5074ad-dirty (upstream-pr-138)`). - [ ] Click the copy button — build string is on the clipboard and a "Copied to clipboard" toast appears. - [ ] `make install` on `main` — version shows git describe output without a branch suffix. - [ ] Release build (`make install RELEASE=1`) — version row still renders correctly from packaged metadata.

title: feat: Add repeatable performance benchmarks for clipboard dialog open latency
body:
### Problem

There are several recent PRs focused on performance / responsiveness, but they do not appear to include repeatable performance measurements showing before/after impact:

- #130
- #135
- #138

This makes it hard to tell whether a PR actually improves startup/open latency, or whether it just changes the implementation in a way that feels faster on one machine.

This is especially important because there is already user-facing performance concern tracked in
* #72

### Description

Add a small, repeatable performance test / benchmark feature to the test framework so performance-related PRs can report objective before/after numbers.

At minimum, it should measure opening the clipboard dialog in these scenarios:

| Scenario | Clipboard history size | Expected measurement |
|---|---:|---|
| Cold open, empty DB | 0 entries | Time to first usable/open dialog |
| Warm open, empty DB | 0 entries | Time to reopen after first initialization |
| Cold open, large DB | 1,000 entries | Time to first usable/open dialog |
| Warm open, large DB | 1,000 entries | Time to reopen after first initialization |

The 1,000-entry case should use a committed fixture/example file in the test framework so results are consistent across PRs.

This would let future performance PRs include clear before/after output like:

```text
Before:
  cold open, 0 entries:      XXX ms
  warm open, 0 entries:      XXX ms
  cold open, 1000 entries:   XXX ms
  warm open, 1000 entries:   XXX ms

After:
  cold open, 0 entries:      XXX ms
  warm open, 0 entries:      XXX ms
  cold open, 1000 entries:   XXX ms
  warm open, 1000 entries:   XXX ms
```

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Add a repeatable way to measure clipboard dialog open latency.
- [ ] Measure both cold open and warm open.
- [ ] Include a 0-entry fixture/test case.
- [ ] Include a 1,000-entry fixture/test case.
- [ ] Print or record timings in a format that can be pasted into PR descriptions.
- [ ] Document how contributors should run the benchmark.
- [ ] Future performance PRs can include before/after numbers using the same benchmark.

### Alternative Solutions

A simpler first step could be a manual benchmark command or test helper that prints these timings locally, even if it is not initially enforced in CI.

For example:

```bash
./run-perf-test --entries 0
./run-perf-test --entries 1000
```

Another option would be to add benchmark logging to an existing test path first, then later promote it into CI once the numbers are stable enough.

#### Additional Context

Related recent performance PRs without repeatable before/after benchmark output:

- #130
- #135
- #138

Related performance / startup / workflow-latency issues:

- #72 - GNOME freezes for a few seconds when the clipboard is opened, especially after large text or screenshots.
- #128 - Initial clipboard open is slow: first invocation after login takes 2-3 seconds, while subsequent invocations are almost instant. This maps directly to cold-open vs warm-open benchmarking.
- #139 - Large clipboard history can freeze the GNOME session during login. This supports having a large-history fixture, such as 1,000 entries.
- #127 - SQLite backend can freeze GNOME Shell on login while JSON backend works normally. This suggests benchmarks may need to account for backend differences.
- #74 - Older report of GNOME freezing on login with Copyous enabled.
- #122 - Describes the full dialog workflow as slower for batch clipboard use, which is relevant to measuring user-visible latency.

The main goal is not to block performance work, but to make it easy for contributors to prove before/after impact with repeatable numbers.

title: 🚀 perf: ⚡ perf: optimize cold-boot startup and dialog open path
body:
Defer all heavy work in `enable()` to
`GLib.idle_add(GLib.PRIORITY_LOW, ...)` after the shell emits `startup-complete`, and lazy-import heavy modules
(`ThemeManager`, `ClipboardDialog`, `ClipboardIndicator`, `GDA`, etc.) in parallel via dynamic `import()`.

This eliminates the vanilla dock flash during cold boot, since the extension no longer competes with Mutter for the main loop during shell startup.

Clipboard history loading
-------------------------

Bulk-load the initial clipboard history through a new `loadEntries()` / `loadItems()` path that appends items directly. The database already returns rows ordered by descending datetime, so the previous `addEntry()` loop was unnecessarily expensive:

- linear scan per insertion
- per-item `updateSearch()`
- per-item `updateVisible()`
- per-item pseudoclass updates

Resulting in O(N²) behavior during startup.

Also remove the premature `search()` call from the dialog constructor and execute it once after the bulk load completes.

Lazy dialog layout
-------------------------

Make dialog layout fully lazy:

- `updatePosition()` and `updateMargins()` are no longer called from the constructor
- a `_layoutDirty` flag tracks pending layout updates
- layout is applied on first `open()` (or immediately if already open)

After bulk loading, schedule a hidden `preWarm()` pass at idle time to force a first allocation while the dialog is still invisible, so the first user-triggered open does not pay the layout cost from scratch.

Additional optimizations
-------------------------

- Reduce the open animation duration from 150ms to 100ms for snappier feedback.

- Cache `Intl.Collator` at module scope in `searchEntry.ts` so `localeContains()` no longer allocates a new collator per call. Previously, one collator was created per item, per text field, on every search keystroke.

- In `ClipboardItem.updateHeader()`, skip the `layout_manager` swap and `set_child_above_sibling()` call when the header visibility state has not changed, and only replace the layout manager when its type differs.

  This avoids allocating a new `Clutter.BoxLayout` per item during the initial bulk load.

title: Bracketed paste broken in modern terminals (Alacritty, Ghostty) — paste outputs literal "6~"
body:
### Description

When Copyous is enabled, pasting into terminals that support bracketed paste mode (Alacritty, Ghostty) fails — instead of the actual clipboard content, the paste outputs the literal string `6~`.

This appears related to how Copyous re-injects clipboard content. Bash/zsh in those terminals receives the bracketed-paste escape markers as literal text instead of as control sequences, which suggests the markers are being stored in clipboard history and re-emitted as plain content rather than being stripped or properly re-emitted as control bytes.

### Expected Behavior

When Copyous is enabled, pasting into terminals that support bracketed paste mode (Alacritty, Ghostty) fails — instead of the actual clipboard content, the paste outputs the literal string `6~`.

The clipboard markers (`\e[200~` ... `\e[201~`) appear to be mishandled on re-injection.

**Expected:** the copied text is pasted.
**Actual:** the literal string `6~` is pasted.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Fresh Ubuntu 26.04 install
2. Install Copyous from GNOME Extensions
3. Install Alacritty (`sudo apt install alacritty`) — issue also reproduces with Ghostty
4. Copy any text (e.g. `hello world`) from any source
5. In Alacritty, press Ctrl+Shift+V

title: fix: prevent grab race condition during close animation
body: Add `_closing` flag to block `open()` calls during the 150ms close animation. Without this guard, rapid shortcut presses could trigger `pushModal()` before `popModal()` from the previous close animation ran, corrupting Mutter's keyboard state machine and causing all modifier keys (Meta, Ctrl, Alt) to stop working.

title: fix: bundle highlight.js during build
body:
## Problem
The extension fails to load with the following error:

JS ERROR: ImportError: Unable to load file async from:
file:///home/user/.local/share/copyous@boerdereinar.dev/highlight.min.js
(No such file or directory)

This happens because highlight.min.js is required at runtime but is
never downloaded or included during the build process.

## Fix
Added a Makefile rule that:
- Downloads highlight.min.js from cdnjs during build
- Verifies the SHA512 checksum against the value already defined in constants.ts
- Places it in dist/thirdparty/ so it gets bundled with the extension

## Tested on
- Arch Linux, GNOME 50, Wayland

title: update pl.po
Avoided redundant work in clipboard hot paths to improve extension speed
body:
Made copyous faster by making the changes below:
  - Reused expensive Intl.Collator, Intl.Segmenter, TextDecoder, and TextEncoder instances instead of recreating them repeatedly in src/lib/ui/searchEntry.ts:18, src/lib/ui/components/contentInfo.ts:17, and src/
    lib/misc/clipboard.ts:21.
  - Avoided duplicate clipboard MIME-type reads during clipboard ownership changes in src/lib/misc/clipboard.ts:248.
  - Stopped rerunning item search on irrelevant entry notifications like datetime changes, while keeping search updates for content/tag/type/title/metadata changes in src/lib/ui/clipboardScrollContainer.ts:123.
  - Reduced temporary arrays in search title matching and database pruning in src/lib/ui/searchEntry.ts:84 and src/lib/database/memory.ts:111.
  - Replaced line counting via split('\n') with a simple scan to avoid allocating an array for large text in src/lib/ui/components/contentInfo.ts:42.

I noticed a significant improvement when testing it.

title: SQLite backend freezes GNOME Shell on login, while JSON backend works normally
body:
### Description

When Copyous is configured to use the SQLite backend, GNOME Shell freezes during login for my user account.

The login initially appears to proceed normally: after entering the password, the desktop starts loading, but GNOME Shell freezes around the overview/desktop transition. In some attempts it results in a black screen with only the mouse cursor visible.

Disabling Copyous allows the same user account to log in normally. Re-enabling Copyous after switching its backend from SQLite to JSON also works normally. This strongly suggests the issue is specific to the SQLite/libgda backend rather than Copyous as a whole.

The current working configuration is:

```
  org.gnome.shell.extensions.copyous database-backend 'json'

  With database-backend set to sqlite, the login freeze is reproducible.
```

### Expected Behavior

Copyous should not freeze or block GNOME Shell during login when using the SQLite backend.

The SQLite backend should behave like the JSON backend from a GNOME Shell stability perspective: the extension should load successfully, and GNOME Shell should remain responsive after login.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install and enable Copyous 2.0.1.
2. Configure Copyous to use the SQLite backend:
     `gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.copyous database-backend 'sqlite'`
3. Log out of the GNOME session.
4. Try to log back into the same user account.
5. GNOME Shell starts loading, then freezes around the overview/desktop transition, or shows a black screen with only the mouse cursor.
6. Disable Copyous, or switch the backend to JSON:
`gsettings set org.gnome.shell.extensions.copyous database-backend 'json'`
7. Log in again.
8. GNOME Shell loads normally and Copyous works with the JSON backend.

### Extension Version

2.0.1

### Environment

- Session type: Wayland

title: Allow disabling HTTP(s) URL preview
body:
### Problem

When you copy an HTTP/HTTPS URL, Copyous makes a request to that URL to display a preview. This can lead to several problems:

* confidentiality/privacy issue (if the URL contains trackers or points to "unfriendly" locations)
* it can makes one-time URL unusable when pasted in the browser (already used by Copyous)
* it can trigger unwanted actions
* it can be dangerous if pointing on a neferious ressource...

### Description

It would be nice to have an option to disable the URL preview feature. :)

### Alternative Solutions

It may also be possible to add an allow-list for some website/pattern too (so having an option to ["disable", "enable", "allow only whitelisted"] URL preview). but an option to completely disabling the feature is the more important need.

title: Auto-paste does not work after selecting clipboard entry (GNOME 50 / Wayland)
Fix panel icon left-click not opening clipboard dialog on GNOME 50
body:
### Problem

On GNOME Shell 50 (Ubuntu 26.04), left-clicking the Copyous panel indicator icon does not open the clipboard dialog. Instead, it opens the popup menu (Incognito Mode / Clear History /
  Settings). The keyboard shortcut (Shift+Super+V) works correctly.

  This is caused by GNOME 50 changing PanelMenu.Button to use Clutter.ClickGesture (added via add_action()) instead of vfunc_event() for click handling (introduced in gnome-shell commit
  80bc9d77, MR #3912). Since Clutter dispatches actions before actor vfuncs, the built-in ClickGesture consumes the button-press event and toggles the popup menu before
  vfunc_button_press_event in ClipboardIndicator (lib/ui/indicator.js:225) can intercept it. The vfunc_touch_event override is similarly unreachable.

### Description

The fix is to detect GNOME 50+ and disable the built-in _clickGesture on the PanelMenu.Button, replacing it with a Clutter.ClickAction that routes:
  - Left-click → open-dialog (clipboard dialog)
  - Middle-click → open preferences
  - Right-click → toggle popup menu (Incognito / Clear / Settings)

  This preserves the existing vfunc_button_press_event and vfunc_touch_event overrides as fallbacks for GNOME 49 and below.

### Alternative Solutions

1. Pass dontCreateMenu = true to the PanelMenu.Button constructor and manage the popup menu entirely manually — more invasive, breaks the existing right-click menu setup.
  2. Use a Clutter.ClickGesture with set_recognize_on_press(true) instead of Clutter.ClickAction — functionally equivalent but ClickAction is simpler since it provides get_button()
  directly and doesn't require gesture state management.
  3. Override vfunc_event() instead — would work on GNOME 49 but still wouldn't fire on GNOME 50 since the gesture consumes the event before any actor vfunc.

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Quick "cycle" and notification for selected clipboard item like in https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/779/clipboard-indicator/
body:
### Problem

In previous extensions (like [Clipboard Indicator](https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/779/clipboard-indicator/)), it was possible to cycle through the history "in place." The current workflow requires opening the full dialog, navigating with arrow keys, and pressing Enter.

This introduces several friction points:
- Hand Movement: Requires moving from the primary keys/mouse to the arrow keys.
- Visual Distraction: The full dialog interrupts the workspace for quick, successive pastes.
- Slower "Batch" Work: For users who copy 3 items and want to paste them one after another using Ctrl+V -> Next Item -> Ctrl+V, the current dialog-heavy process is significantly slower.

### Description

Add discrete "Select Next" and "Select Previous" actions that can be bound to global shortcuts (e.g., Super+V / Super+Shift+V). This would allow users to cycle through the clipboard history stack and paste items sequentially without opening the full history UI.

What would help in my workflows are:
1. **Dedicated Shortcuts:** Add two new keybinding options in settings:
   - **Select Next Item:** Moves the active clipboard selection down the stack.
   - **Select Previous Item:** Moves the active clipboard selection up the stack.
2. **Wrap-around Logic:** If the user reaches the end of the history, the selection should wrap back to the first item (and vice-versa).
3. **Optional notification:** When cycling via these shortcuts, show a small temporary notification or OSD indicating which text/item is now active.
4. **Separation of Concerns:** Keep these cycling actions independent of the "Open Clipboard Dialog" action, allowing a workflow like:
   - `Super+V`: Next item (Quick cycle)
   - `Super+Shift+V`: Previous item (Quick cycle)
   - `Super+Ctrl+V`: Open full dialog (For deep history search)

While the setting "Open/select next item" exists, it is missing a "Select previous" counterpart, and it currently forces the dialog to open, rather than allowing for silent cycling in the background with a simple notification. This requires additional keystroke to dismiss/accept the item. I noticed my workflow got significantly slower without hose shortcuts.

### Alternative Solutions

_No response_

feat: backport to GNOME 46 (libadwaita 1.5 / GJS ES2022)
body:
## Backport: GNOME Shell 46 compatibility

### Summary

This PR adds backward compatibility for **GNOME Shell 46** (Ubuntu 24.04 LTS) by replacing APIs that were introduced in GNOME 47+ (libadwaita 1.6) and GNOME 48+. All changes are conditional or use equivalent older APIs, preserving full functionality on newer GNOME versions.

### Motivation

GNOME Shell 46 ships with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, which will be supported until 2029. Copyous currently targets GNOME 48–50, leaving LTS users unable to use the extension. This backport addresses that gap with minimal, targeted changes.

### Changes

#### Runtime (GNOME Shell)

| Issue | GNOME 46 API | GNOME 48+ API | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TypeError: this.getLogger is not a function` | `getLogger?.() ?? console` fallback | `Extension.getLogger()` | `extension.ts`, `actions.ts`, `dependencies.ts` |
| `No property orientation on StBoxLayout` | `vertical: true/false` | `orientation: Clutter.Orientation.*` | 8 UI files |
| `global.compositor.disable_unredirect is not a function` | `Meta.disable_unredirect_for_display(global.display)` | `global.compositor.disable_unredirect()` | `clipboardDialog.ts` |
| `Intl.Segmenter is not a constructor` (drops all plain text clipboard entries) | `Array.from()` / `String.split(/\s+/)` | `Intl.Segmenter` | `clipboard.ts`, `contentInfo.ts` |

#### Preferences (libadwaita)

| Issue | GNOME 46 replacement | Requires | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Adw.ToggleGroup is not a constructor` | `Gtk.ToggleButton` with radio group | libadwaita ≥ 1.6 | `profiles.ts` |
| `Adw.ButtonRow is not a constructor` | `Adw.ActionRow` with `activatable: true` | libadwaita ≥ 1.6 | `actionsGroup.ts`, `actionsPage.ts` |
| `Adw.Spinner is not a constructor` | `Gtk.Spinner` | libadwaita ≥ 1.6 | `dependenciesSettings.ts` |
| `Adw.SpinnerPaintable is not a constructor` | `Gtk.Spinner` | libadwaita ≥ 1.6 | `dependencies.ts` |

#### Metadata

- Added `"46"` and `"47"` to `shell-version` in `metadata.json`

### Testing

- Built and tested on **Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS** with **GNOME Shell 46.0**
- Extension loads without errors (`State: ACTIVE`)
- Clipboard capture works for all content types (text, links, images, files)
- Preferences dialog loads fully — all tabs functional (General, Customization, Shortcuts, Actions)
- Profile switching (Default / Compact / Custom) works correctly
- Verified zero `JS ERROR` messages in GNOME Shell journal

### Compatibility

These changes are safe for all supported GNOME versions:
- **GNOME 46–47**: Uses the fallback/replacement APIs introduced in this PR
- **GNOME 48–50**: Existing code paths remain unchanged (conditional checks used where applicable)

title: fix(indicator): restore left-click dialog open on GNOME 50+
body:
GNOME 50 changed PanelMenu.Button to use an internal ClickGesture that toggles the menu on press, causing left-click and right-click on the indicator to trigger the same menu action.

Configure the internal panel click gesture to require BUTTON_SECONDARY on GNOME 50+. This keeps right-click opening the indicator menu while restoring left-click behavior to open the clipboard dialog as intended.

Fixes #108

title: Disabling Pin Feature(s)
body:
### Problem

Hello! I just found this after trying out several other clipboard managers; I am very impressed with Copyous. This one is my favorite!

I'm coming from a primarily Windows and MacOS background and now using Fedora. After selecting an item from Clipboard History, my 'instinctive' workflow has been hitting Alt+Tab to tab out of the Clipboard History window.

With Copyous, I open the clipboard history via `Super+V` and exit/tab out of Copyous with `Alt+Tab`. However, pressing `Alt` alone triggers the "Pinned Search" which then makes it so that I cannot tab out. Since I don’t use pinning feature, this behavior feels unnecessary and gets in the way.

tldr it's not possible to `Alt+Tab` out of the Copyous clipboard manager for the `Currently` reasons below.

### Description

Because I do not use the feature, it would be very helpful to have more flexibility around it:

Currently: 
- `Alt` switches to "Toggled Pinned Search"
- It is not possible to change nor disable `Alt` keyboard shortcut for "Toggled Pinned Search"
- It is not possible to disable the Pinned feature entirely.

Feature Request:
- 'Ability to disable the `Alt` shortcut for “Toggle Pinned Search”
- 'Option to remap that shortcut to a different key
- 'Option to completely disable the Pinned Items feature


Thank you for continuing to maintain this amazing tool!

### Description

On Ubuntu 26.04 / GNOME 50, both left‑click and right‑click on the panel icon trigger the same action—opening the configuration/clear menu—so the clipboard history cannot be opened from the icon and is only accessible through the keyboard shortcut.

### Expected Behavior

On Ubuntu 25.10 / GNOME 49:

- Left‑click on the panel icon → opens the clipboard history.
- Right‑click → shows the configuration menu and the “clear history” option.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Install Copyous on Ubuntu 26.04 with GNOME 50
2. Left‑click the panel icon.
3. Observe that the history does not open; instead, the configuration menu appears. 
4. Right‑click the icon and confirm the same result.

### Extension Version

2.0

### Environment

Affected versions: Ubuntu 26.04 (development) / GNOME 50
Working as expected in: Ubuntu 25.10 / GNOME 49

title: GNOME Shell freeze on login when using GDA 6 SQLite database
body:
### Description

On login, GNOME Shell freezes completely and never recovers, requiring a hard reboot. The freeze only occurs at fresh boot when Copyous is enabled and configured to use the GDA-backed SQLite database. Enabling the **in-memory database** option resolves the issue entirely.

**Analysis (Claude's hypothesis)**

While troubleshooting this issue I had Claude Code read the logs and look at the extension and it found the following:

In `lib/misc/gda.js`, the `open_async` function for GDA 6 constructs a Promise with no timeout and no rejection path:

```javascript
export function open_async(connection) {
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
        if ('open_async' in connection) {
            // Gda 6
            connection.set_main_context(null, GLib.MainContext.ref_thread_default());
            connection.open_async((_cnc, _jobId, result) => resolve(result));
        } else {
            // Gda 5
            resolve(connection.open());
        }
    });
}
```

If the `open_async` callback is never invoked, this Promise never resolves, and `await open_async(...)` in `GdaDatabase.init()` blocks permanently — which, in GNOME Shell's single-threaded JS environment, means the entire shell hangs.

The freeze only occurring at boot suggests that under the resource contention typical of early boot (cold filesystem cache, many services starting simultaneously), GDA 6's async connection opening stalls or deadlocks internally in a way that doesn't happen in a settled, running session. However, I don't have visibility into GDA 6's internals, so the exact mechanism on that side is speculation.

The lack of any timeout or fallback in the Promise means any such stall becomes an unrecoverable freeze.




### Expected Behavior

GNOME shell starts with the extension enabled

### Reproduction Steps

1. Enable Copyous with the default GDA SQLite database (not in-memory)
2. Reboot the system
3. Log in 
4. GNOME Shell freezes on the grey screen and never completes loading

**Does not reproduce** when:
- Enabling the extension in an already-running session
- Using the in-memory database option

**Workaround**

Enable **in-memory database** in Copyous settings. This bypasses GDA/SQLite initialization entirely at startup. The trade-off is that clipboard history is not persisted across reboots.

### Extension Version

1.3.0

### Environment

**GNOME Shell version:** 49.4 (Mutter 49.4)
**GDA version:** 6.0
**OS:** Arch Linux (CachyOS), Wayland session

title: [Feature Request/Bug] Support for File URIs and x-special/gnome-copied-files MIME type
body:
### Description

Hello,

First of all, thank you for this amazing extension. It is by far the most polished and "native-feeling" clipboard manager for GNOME Wayland.
Currently, Copyous seems to have trouble handling files copied from Nautilus (GNOME Files). When I copy a file, it appears in the history. However, if I copy something else and then try to re-select that file from the Copyous history to paste it elsewhere in the file manager, the "Paste" action is unavailable or nothing happens.

### Expected Behavior

When selecting a previously copied file from the history, Copyous should re-assert the x-special/gnome-copied-files (and potentially text/uri-list) MIME types so that Nautilus can perform the paste operation correctly.

Thank you for your time and for this great tool!

### Reproduction Steps

- Open Nautilus (GNOME Files) and navigate to any folder.

- Copy a file (e.g., test_document.pdf) using Ctrl+C or the right-click menu.
Observe that the file appears correctly in the Copyous history list.

- Copy any string of text from another application (e.g., a URL from a browser or a line from the Terminal).

- Open the Copyous interface and select the previously copied file from the history to make it the active clipboard item again.

- Try to Paste (Ctrl+V) that file into a different folder in Nautilus.

- Actual Result:
The "Paste" option in Nautilus is either greyed out (disabled) or nothing happens when pressing Ctrl+V. The file is not copied.

### Extension Version

1.3.0 (7)

### Environment

Environment:

- Distro: Debian Trixie (Stable)

title: Fix database schema migration causing duplicate column error
body:
Fixed a critical bug in the database schema migration logic that caused
the "duplicate column name: title" error during initialization.

Problem:
When creating a new database (version 0), the code would:
1. Create the 'clipboard' table without the 'title' column
2. Fall through to case 1 due to missing break statement
3. Attempt to add the 'title' column with ALTER TABLE
4. Fail with "duplicate column name: title" error

This prevented the clipboard history from persisting and forced the
extension to use in-memory storage only.

Solution:
1. Added 'title' column to the initial CREATE TABLE statement (case 0)
2. Added break statement to prevent fall-through to case 1
3. Updated case 1 comment to clarify it's for migrating existing databases

Now the migration works correctly:
- New installations (version 0): Create table with 'title' column included
- Existing databases (version 1): Add 'title' column via ALTER TABLE
- No duplicate column errors

title: Switch to next Item when Dialog already open
body:
### Problem

When I open the Clipboard Dialog with the shortcut (in my case Ctrl + F12), I have to move my right hand to the cursor buttons, select my item, and then insert/copy it via Return. I have to move my hand two times.

### Description

After opening the Clipboard Dialog with the shortcut, pressing the shortcut again shouldn't close it, but jump to the next item. Then I can insert the item via Return. I only have to move my hand once. 

In my case: Ctrl + F12 -> Dialog opens -> Ctrl + F12 -> the next item in line is selected -> Return

This would make things easier, if this could be configured. 

### Alternative Solutions

I think two things would be required to make this work:

1. An option to activate said bevaviour -> do not close the dialog when pressed again, but select the next item
2. An option to change the shortcuts for navigating in the dialog (E.g.: Ctrl+F12 -> next item, Ctrl+F11 -> previous Item)

### Additional Context

Clipboard Indicator does this in a similar way.
https://extensions.gnome.org/extension/779/clipboard-indicator/

I just press Ctrl+F12 x-amount of times, then i paste.

body:

Fixes #75

title: Option to show the clipboard button in the System Menu.
body: ### Problem There's lots of padding between items by default and it would look nice in the System Menu. This is implemented by "display-brightness-ddcutil@themightydeity.github.com`. ### Description It just would have looked way nicer as that way the System Menu items have less padding looking more cohesive. ### Alternative Solutions _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_

title: Highlight.js system install
body:
Hi, thanks for making this extension I loved pano but was really sad that it's been abandoned/archived.

I packaged this extension for archlinux (https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/gnome-shell-extension-copyous) but I'm wondering if it would be possible for me to automatically install highlight.js somewhere into the system path where the extension is installed (e.g., somewhere under `/usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/copyous@boerdereinar.dev/`) so that a user doesn't have to perform any additional steps other than install the extension.

I hope that's clear the tl;dr is I would like a system path where I can install highlight.js to make it automatically available to all users of the system instead of each user needing to download it to their home directory. Thanks!

Cheers

title: GNOME Shell keeps NVIDIA GPU active when Copyous is enabled
body:
### Description

My device uses a hybrid graphics setup with NVIDIA and Intel GPUs. I have configured Automatic Suspend (enabling RTD3 Power Management) for the NVIDIA GPU to save power, while using the Intel integrated graphics to drive the GNOME session.

Everything works as expected, but I discovered that as soon as Copyous is enabled, GNOME Shell occupies the GPU and keeps it in an "active" state. I monitor the GPU status using: `cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:02:00.0/power/runtime_status`

The moment Copyous is turned on, GNOME Shell freezes for about 2 seconds, after which the GPU starts up and remains active. Furthermore, even after disabling Copyous, GNOME Shell continues to occupy the GPU.

This is a difficult issue to debug, and I am unsure about the consistent reproducibility across different environments, so I am submitting this issue to seek guidance. Given that Copyous is a rewrite of Pano, I tested Pano as well; it does not trigger this behavior, and the GPU remains in the suspended state as intended.

### Expected Behavior

The NVIDIA GPU should remain in a suspended state when Copyous is enabled. GNOME Shell should not trigger the GPU to activate.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Configure a system with NVIDIA/Intel hybrid graphics and enable RTD3 Power Management for the NVIDIA GPU.
2. Verify the GPU is suspended using `cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:02:00.0/power/runtime_status` (should return `suspended`).
3. Enable the Copyous extension.
4. You will see a brief system freeze (~2 seconds) in the GNOME Shell.
5. Check the GPU status again; it will now show as active and remain in that state for the whole session even if the extension is subsequently disabled.

### Extension Version

1.3.0 (7)

- GNOME Version: 49.2
- Distro: Arch Linux
- Distro Version: rolling

title: Option to disable primary paste from everywhere
body:
### Problem

I personally have had troubles with feature for years, and I believe it's a security hole and huge privacy risk for Linux. 

ALSO please ignore this feature request if you don't want to implement it.

### Description

I'm not sure how it'd be possible to disable this function system-wide.
I've disabled primary paste from GTK and Qt but it still works in other apps.

### Alternative Solutions

Detect when text is selected and wipe the primary paste, this should be possible trough gnome-shell.

### Additional Context

I've been struggling against this feature for years, I end up pasting when I don't mean to.
Gnome disabling it by default in GTK soon made me go on a hunt again to find a way to disable it system wide, but I couldn't find a solution no matter the search query.

title: Light / dark mode out of sync with host
body:
### Description

Despite `gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme` correctly reflecting the current system preference (e.g. `prefer-light`), Copyous intermittently fails to follow it. In these cases, the system is on Light Style while Copyous remains on Dark Style, even though its theme setting is configured to “System”.

### Expected Behavior

Copyous would follow the system's dark or light mode when set to use "System" under "Customization" > "Theme" > "Theme".

Switch from Dark Style to Light Style via the toggle in the Quick Settings.

title: Add Simplified Chinese translation
Add "Title" Field to Paste List Items in Paste Manager
body:
### Problem

Currently, pastes are displayed in a list, often showing only a text snippet. When saving multiple similar items (e.g., two different passwords), it's easy to forget which one corresponds to which account or service later.

### Description

The current Paste Manager extension is very useful for viewing clipboard history. However, to improve its usability for managing multiple items (like different passwords, codes, or notes), I propose adding a simple "Title" or "Label" field to each saved paste.

### Alternative Solutions

Allow users to optionally add a custom title/label (e.g., "Gmail Password", "API Key for Project X") when an item is saved to the paste list, or to edit the title afterward. This title would be displayed prominently in the list view, making items much easier to identify and search for at a glance.

### Additional Context

This small addition would greatly enhance the extension's functionality as a knowledge snippet or credential manager, helping users organize and retrieve pasted information quickly and accurately.

Thank you for considering this improvement.

title: Duplicate "Fill" options in position dropdown menu
body: ### Description In the Dialog settings panel, the dropdown menu for position settings displays duplicate "Fill" entries. When opening the dropdown (visible in the Vertical Position context), three separate "Fill" options appear in the list instead of unique position values. The dropdown currently shows: This appears to be a UI bug where the same option is rendered multiple times, which could cause confusion and potentially unexpected behavior when selecting options. ### Expected Behavior The dropdown menu should display only unique position options, such as: Top Center Bottom Fill Each option should appear exactly once in the list. ### Reproduction Steps 1. Open Copyous settings/preferences 2. Navigate to the Dialog section 3. Click on the Vertical Position dropdown 4.
